statement: A symbol representing a fixed element of the domain D. (Variant 7)

title: Function Symbol (FOL Def 450)
statement: A symbol assigned a mapping from D^n to D. (Variant 7)

title: Predicate Symbol (FOL Def 451)
statement: A symbol assigned a relation on D^n. (Variant 7)

title: Term (FOL Def 452)
statement: Defined inductively: variables and constants are terms; f(t1...tn) is a term if f is an n-ary function symbol and ti are terms. (Variant 7)

title: Atomic Formula (FOL Def 453)
statement: P(t1...tn) or t1=t2 where P is a predicate and ti are terms. (Variant 7)

title: Well-Formed Formula (WFF) (FOL Def 454)
statement: Built from atomic formulas using connectives and quantifiers. (Variant 7)

title: Free Variable (FOL Def 455)
statement: A variable occurrence not in the scope of a quantifier. (Variant 7)

title: Bound Variable (FOL Def 456)
statement: A variable occurrence within the scope of a quantifier. (Variant 7)

title: Sentence (FOL Def 457)
statement: A formula with no free variables. (Variant 7)

title: Structure (FOL Def 458)
statement: A pair (D, I) where D is a non-empty domain and I is an interpretation function. (Variant 7)

title: Interpretation (FOL Def 459)
statement: A mapping from symbols to domain elements, functions, and relations. (Variant 7)

title: Variable Assignment (FOL Def 460)
statement: A function v: Var -> D. (Variant 7)

title: Satisfaction relation (FOL Def 461)
statement: M, v |= phi, defined inductively on the structure of phi. (Variant 7)

title: Model (FOL Def 462)
statement: A structure M such that M |= phi for all sentences phi in a theory T. (Variant 7)

title: Validity (FOL Def 463)
statement: A formula is valid if it is satisfied by every structure and every assignment. (Variant 7)

title: Satisfiability (FOL Def 464)
statement: A formula is satisfiable if there exists a structure and assignment that satisfies it. (Variant 7)

title: Logical Consequence (FOL Def 465)
statement: T |= phi if every model of T is a model of phi. (Variant 7)

title: Prenex Normal Form (FOL Def 466)
statement: A formula where all quantifiers appear at the beginning. (Variant 7)
patterns: What is a Prenex Normal Form?

title: Skolem Normal Form (FOL Def 467)
statement: A prenex formula with only universal quantifiers, using Skolem constants/functions. (Variant 7)
patterns: What is a Skolem Normal Form?

title: Arity (FOL Def 468)
statement: The number of arguments a function or predicate symbol takes. (Variant 7)

title: Signature (FOL Def 469)
statement: The set of non-logical symbols (constants, functions, predicates) and their arities. (Variant 7)

title: Substructure (FOL Def 470)
statement: A structure whose domain is a subset of another and whose operations are restrictions. (Variant 7)

title: Isomorphism (FOL Def 471)
statement: A bijective mapping between structures preserving interpretations. (Variant 7)

title: Elementary Equivalence (FOL Def 472)
statement: Two structures are elementary equivalent if they satisfy the same sentences. (Variant 7)

title: Consistency (FOL Def 473)
statement: A set of sentences is consistent if it has a model. (Variant 7)

title: Completeness of Theory (FOL Def 474)
statement: A theory T is complete if for every sentence phi, T |= phi or T |= not phi. (Variant 7)
patterns: What is a Completeness of Theory?

title: Categoricity (FOL Def 475)
statement: A theory is kappa-categorical if all models of power kappa are isomorphic. (Variant 7)

title: Substitution (FOL Def 476)
statement: Replacing occurrences of a variable with a term, avoiding capture. (Variant 7)

title: Alpha-conversion (FOL Def 477)
statement: Renaming bound variables without changing the meaning of the formula. (Variant 7)

title: Rank of a Formula (FOL Def 478)
statement: The maximum nesting level of operators or quantifiers. (Variant 7)
patterns: What is a Rank of a Formula?

title: Complexity of Formula (FOL Def 479)
statement: The total number of logical symbols in a formula. (Variant 7)
patterns: What is a Complexity of Formula?

title: Universal Closure (FOL Def 480)
statement: The sentence obtained by prefixing a formula with universal quantifiers for all free variables. (Variant 7)

title: Existential Closure (FOL Def 481)
statement: The sentence obtained by prefixing a formula with existential quantifiers for all free variables. (Variant 7)

title: Henkin Set (FOL Def 482)
statement: A set of sentences that contains witnesses for every existential sentence. (Variant 7)

title: Witness (FOL Def 483)
statement: A constant c such that phi(c) holds if exists x phi(x) holds. (Variant 7)

title: Theory (FOL Def 484)
statement: A set of sentences closed under logical consequence. (Variant 7)

title: Expansion (FOL Def 485)
statement: Adding new symbols to a signature while keeping the domain and original interpretations. (Variant 7)

title: Reduct (FOL Def 486)
statement: Removing symbols from a signature. (Variant 7)

title: Atomic Theory (FOL Def 487)
statement: The set of all atomic sentences and their negations satisfied by a structure. (Variant 7)

title: Elementary Substructure (FOL Def 488)
statement: A substructure that satisfies the same formulas (with parameters) as the parent structure. (Variant 7)

title: Ultraproduct (FOL Def 489)
statement: A construction of a new structure from a family of structures and an ultrafilter. (Variant 7)

title: Compactness Property (FOL Def 490)
statement: A logic has the compactness property if satisfiability is determined by finite subsets. (Variant 7)

title: Löwenheim Number (FOL Def 491)
statement: The smallest cardinal kappa such that every satisfiable sentence has a model of size kappa. (Variant 7)

title: Skolem Function (FOL Def 492)
statement: A function that replaces an existential quantifier, depending on previous universal variables. (Variant 7)

title: Skolem Constant (FOL Def 493)
statement: A Skolem function of arity 0. (Variant 7)

title: Herbrand Universe (FOL Def 494)
statement: The set of all ground terms in a signature. (Variant 7)

title: Herbrand Base (FOL Def 495)
statement: The set of all ground atomic formulas. (Variant 7)

title: Herbrand Interpretation (FOL Def 496)
statement: An interpretation whose domain is the Herbrand universe. (Variant 7)

title: Literal (FOL Def 497)
statement: An atomic formula or its negation. (Variant 7)

title: Clause (FOL Def 498)
statement: A disjunction of literals. (Variant 7)

title: Decidability (FOL Def 499)
statement: The property of a set of sentences being recursive. (Variant 7)

title: Semi-decidability (FOL Def 500)
statement: The property of a set of sentences being recursively enumerable. (Variant 7)

title: Finite Model Failure Counterexample 1
statement: Certain formulas have only infinite models. (Instance 1)
refutation: Formula: forall x,y,z (P(x,y) & P(y,z) -> P(x,z)) & forall x (~P(x,x)) & forall x exists y P(x,y). D=N, P=<. No finite model. (Assignment i=1)

title: Skolemization Difference Counterexample 2
statement: phi and Skolem(phi) are not logically equivalent, only equi-satisfiable. (Instance 2)
refutation: phi = exists x P(x). Skolem(phi) = P(c). In structure M where P={0}, phi is true. In M' where c=1 and P={0}, Skolem(phi) is false. (Assignment i=2)

title: Substitution Capture Counterexample 3
statement: phi(x) and phi(t) are not equivalent if x is captured. (Instance 3)
refutation: phi(x) = exists y (x != y). t = y. phi(y) = exists y (y != y) which is false, while phi(x) could be true. (Assignment i=3)

title: Empty Domain Counterexample 4
statement: FOL assumes non-empty domains. In empty domains, forall x P(x) is true but exists x P(x) is false. (Instance 4)
refutation: D={}, forall x P(x) trivially true, exists x P(x) false. Standard FOL axioms forall x phi -> exists x phi fail. (Assignment i=4)

title: Generalization Violation Counterexample 5
statement: If T |- phi(x), then T |- forall x phi(x) only if x is not free in T. (Instance 5)
refutation: T = {P(x)}, phi = P(x). T |- P(x) but T does not imply forall x P(x). D={0,1}, I(P)={0}, v(x)=0. M,v satisfies P(x) but M fails forall x P(x). (Assignment i=5)

title: Quantifier Swap Counterexample 6
statement: forall x exists y P(x,y) does not imply exists y forall x P(x,y). (Instance 6)
refutation: D={0,1}, P={(0,0), (1,1)}. M satisfies forall x exists y P(x,y) but not exists y forall x P(x,y). (Assignment i=6)

refutation: Formula: forall x,y,z (P(x,y) & P(y,z) -> P(x,z)) & forall x (~P(x,x)) & forall x exists y P(x,y). D=N, P=<. No finite model. (Assignment i=331)

title: Skolemization Difference Counterexample 332
statement: phi and Skolem(phi) are not logically equivalent, only equi-satisfiable. (Instance 332)
refutation: phi = exists x P(x). Skolem(phi) = P(c). In structure M where P={0}, phi is true. In M' where c=1 and P={0}, Skolem(phi) is false. (Assignment i=332)

title: Substitution Capture Counterexample 333
statement: phi(x) and phi(t) are not equivalent if x is captured. (Instance 333)
refutation: phi(x) = exists y (x != y). t = y. phi(y) = exists y (y != y) which is false, while phi(x) could be true. (Assignment i=333)

title: Empty Domain Counterexample 334
statement: FOL assumes non-empty domains. In empty domains, forall x P(x) is true but exists x P(x) is false. (Instance 334)
refutation: D={}, forall x P(x) trivially true, exists x P(x) false. Standard FOL axioms forall x phi -> exists x phi fail. (Assignment i=334)

title: Generalization Violation Counterexample 335
statement: If T |- phi(x), then T |- forall x phi(x) only if x is not free in T. (Instance 335)
refutation: T = {P(x)}, phi = P(x). T |- P(x) but T does not imply forall x P(x). D={0,1}, I(P)={0}, v(x)=0. M,v satisfies P(x) but M fails forall x P(x). (Assignment i=335)

title: Quantifier Swap Counterexample 336
statement: forall x exists y P(x,y) does not imply exists y forall x P(x,y). (Instance 336)
refutation: D={0,1}, P={(0,0), (1,1)}. M satisfies forall x exists y P(x,y) but not exists y forall x P(x,y). (Assignment i=336)
